newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 3.057 billion yuan from 4.137 billion yuan on Tuesday with the 20-day contract the most actively traded.

Trading continued to be active despite a fall mainly because more and more domestic banks are now using the interbank market to trade short-term funds following new official measures to control trading on the state debt market, traders said.
Participation of foreign banks in the interbank market trading which started last month also added to the volume, they said.

The China Securities newspaper on Wednesday quoted the central bank governor, Dai Xianglong, as saying China would expand the number of foreign insurance firms and investment banks allowed to operate in the country this year.
Traders said this would add trading volume to the interbank market in the mid-term.
Economic data announced early this week indicated China's inflation continued to fall in the first four months of this year and traders said this would help depress the interbank rates gradually.
Traders said they believed the interbank rates would move narrowly in active trading in the next few days.
